note: Ps69 great lament (corrected; 2nd-longest, dense IB). Human core (29 chars): weary(yaga) crying-out + waiting(yachal); enemies' causeless HATE + LIES; owned FOLLY + wrongs; concern the HOPERS/SEEKERS not be shamed through him; the REPROACH/DISHONOR + ZEAL borne for God; WEPT; PRAYER; broken HEART + DESPAIR + vain LOOKED for pity; AFFLICTED + PAIN; then PRAISE/MAGNIFY/THANKSGIVING, the HUMBLE/NEEDY/SEEKERS GLAD + REVIVEd, those who LOVE God's name. God-qualifiers ~30 (save/deliver/answer/turn/near/redeem/ransom/hide + chesed/faithfulness/mercy; wrath indignation/anger/pour-out; hears/not-despise; save-Zion). Drowning/mire/flood + imprecation (snare/trap/darkened/blotted) + reproach-suffering imagery = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: be weary / faint (yaga - weary with my crying out)
paired with the crying and the waiting for God

'I am WEARY (yaga) with my crying out; my throat is parched' — exhaustion from unanswered prayer; yaga here the fatigue of a soul that has cried until it can cry no more, eyes failing as it waits for God
cry out / call (qara - my crying out)
'weary with my CRYING OUT (qara)' — the ceaseless calling to God; qara here the crying that has worn the psalmist out, the voice of a man in deep waters calling until his throat fails
wait / hope (yachal - my eyes grow dim with waiting for my God)

'My eyes grow dim with WAITING (yachal) for my God' — hope stretched to the edge of failing sight; yachal here the waiting on God that has strained the eyes dim — expectation held even as strength gives out, faith at its most exhausted
hate (sane - those who hate me without cause)
more in number than the hairs of his head
paired with those who attack him with lies
on whom God's indignation is asked to fall (v24)

'More in number than the hairs of my head are those who HATE (sane) me without cause' — the countless, groundless enemies; sane here the causeless hatred (cf John 15:25) surrounding the psalmist — malice with no reason but its own, which God's wrath will answer (v24)
lies / falsehood (sheqer - those who attack me with lies)

'mighty are those who would destroy me, those who attack me with LIES (sheqer)' — false accusation as the enemies' weapon; sheqer here the lies with which the mighty foes assail him, demanding he restore what he never stole (v4) — falsehood pressed as if it were justice
folly / foolishness (ivveleth - you know my folly)
paired with the wrongs he has done

'O God, you KNOW my FOLLY (ivveleth); the wrongs I have done are not hidden from you' — honest confession of real failings even while protesting innocence of the charges; ivveleth here the psalmist's own foolishness, laid open before the God who knows all — no self-righteousness in his plea, only truth
guilt / wrongs done (ashmah - the wrongs I have done)

'the WRONGS I have done (ashmah) are not hidden from you' — the guilt the psalmist owns before God; ashmah here his real faults, acknowledged frankly - his innocence of the enemies' charges does not make him sinless, and he hides nothing from God
hope / wait (qavah - those who hope in you)
paired with those who seek God

'Let not those who HOPE (qavah) in you be put to shame through me' — the psalmist's altruistic dread that his disgrace might discredit the faithful; qavah here the God-hopers whose confidence he fears to shame - his suffering weighed for its effect on others' faith, not just himself
paired with those who hope in God

'let not those who SEEK (baqash) you be brought to dishonor through me' — the God-seekers whom the psalmist fears his plight might dishonor; baqash here the earnest seekers of God, for whose sake he prays his own shame not spread - solidarity of the faithful
reproach (cherpah - for your sake I have borne reproach)
the reproaches that fell on him for God (v9)

'For it is for your sake that I have borne REPROACH (cherpah)' — shame suffered on God's account; cherpah here the reproach the psalmist carries because of his devotion to God - his disgrace bound up with God's, the reproaches of God's revilers falling on him (v9)
dishonor / shame (kelimmah - dishonor has covered my face)
paired with the reproach borne for God
'that DISHONOR (kelimmah) has covered my face' — humiliation veiling the psalmist like a garment; kelimmah here the shame that covers his face, the visible mark of the reproach borne for God's sake
zeal / jealousy (qinah - zeal for your house has consumed me)
paired with the reproaches of God's revilers falling on him

'For ZEAL (qinah) for your house has consumed me' — burning devotion to God's honor that devours the psalmist; qinah here the jealous zeal for God's house that has eaten him up (cited of Christ, John 2:17) - passion for God's glory so total it becomes his suffering, drawing the revilers' reproach onto himself
reproaches (cherpah - the reproaches of those who reproach you fell on me)

'the REPROACHES (cherpah) of those who reproach you have fallen on me' — the insults hurled at God landing on his servant; cherpah here the revilers' scorn of God, borne by the psalmist as his own - identification with God so complete that God's shame becomes his (cited Rom 15:3)
weep (bakah - when I wept and humbled my soul with fasting)
weep and humble the soul (with fasting)
the mourning that became his reproach

'When I WEPT (bakah) and humbled my soul with fasting, it became my reproach' — piety itself turned into an occasion for mockery; bakah here the weeping and fasting of true devotion, which the scoffers twist into a byword - his very humbling before God used against him
prayer (tefillah - my prayer is to you, O LORD)
to the LORD, at an acceptable time
appealing to God's abundant steadfast love
resting on God's steadfast love and saving faithfulness (v13)

'But as for me, my PRAYER (tefillah) is to you, O LORD' — the turn from the scoffers' songs to God; tefillah here the psalmist's recourse against all the mockery - amid drowning and reproach, his prayer rises to God, resting on the abundance of his steadfast love and saving faithfulness (the qualifiers) that he begs to deliver, answer, redeem, and ransom him
heart (leb - reproaches have broken my heart)
issues in despair and vain looking for pity

'Reproaches have BROKEN my HEART (leb), so that I am in despair' — the inner core shattered by scorn; leb here the heart crushed by reproach to the point of despair - the deepest wound of the lament, a broken and hopeless spirit that finds no comforter
be in despair / be sick (anash - I am in despair)
the state of the broken heart

'so that I am in DESPAIR (anash)' — the sickness of a heart with no hope left; anash here the desperate, incurable grief that follows the broken heart - the nadir of the psalm, before the turn to praise
look / wait for (qavah - I looked for pity, but there was none)
the loneliness that deepens the despair

'I LOOKED (qavah) for pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none' — the isolation of the sufferer whom no one consoles; qavah here the vain waiting for human sympathy - the utter aloneness that leaves God as the only refuge
afflicted / poor (ani - but I am afflicted and in pain)
paired with his pain, met by God's salvation
whom God's salvation sets on high (v29)

'But I am AFFLICTED (ani) and in pain; let your salvation, O God, set me on high!' — the low estate that pleads for God's rescue; ani here the poor, afflicted psalmist, whose only hope is that God's salvation (the qualifier) will lift him from the depths - the turn from lament toward trust
'afflicted and in PAIN (keeb)' — the suffering that accompanies the affliction; keeb here the pain of the wounded soul, from which God's salvation is asked to lift him high
praise (halal - I will praise the name of God with a song)
the name of God, with a song
paired with magnifying God with thanksgiving

'I will PRAISE (halal) the name of God with a song' — the vow of praise that answers the depths; halal here the song promised amid affliction - the lament turning to worship even before deliverance is seen, praise that pleases God more than sacrifice (v31)
magnify / make great (gadal - I will magnify him with thanksgiving)

'I will MAGNIFY (gadal) him with thanksgiving' — exalting God in grateful praise; gadal here the making-great of God with thanks - the afflicted soul enlarging God's name, worship as the fruit of hope

'magnify him with THANKSGIVING (todah)' — the grateful offering that exalts God; todah here the thanks the psalmist brings - more pleasing to God than ox or bull (v31), the sacrifice of a grateful heart
humble / afflicted (anav - when the humble see it they will be glad)
paired with their gladness and the seekers' reviving

'When the HUMBLE (anav) see it they will be glad' — the lowly encouraged by the sufferer's deliverance; anav here the humble/afflicted who take heart at God's rescue of one like them - the psalmist's testimony reviving the hearts of the God-seekers
be glad / rejoice (samach - they will be glad)
the gladness of the humble who see

'the humble see it and are GLAD (samach)' — joy spreading from one deliverance to the whole company of the lowly; samach here the gladness the humble share when God saves the afflicted - the sufferer's rescue becomes the community's hope

'you who SEEK (darash) God, let your hearts revive' — the God-seekers called to fresh life; darash here the earnest seekers of God, whose flagging hearts are quickened by seeing him hear the needy - the psalmist's rescue reviving all who seek God
revive / live (chayah - let your hearts revive)
the reviving of the seekers' hearts

'you who seek God, let your hearts REVIVE (chayah)' — the heart brought back to life; chayah here the reviving of the seekers' hearts - drooping faith quickened again by God's care for the needy, the fainting made to live
needy / poor (ebyon - the LORD hears the needy)
whom the LORD hears and does not despise (v33)

'For the LORD hears the NEEDY (ebyon) and does not despise his own people who are prisoners' — the poor and imprisoned whom God attends; ebyon here the destitute, assured that God hears them (the qualifier) and never scorns his captive people - the ground of hope for all the afflicted
love (aheb - those who love his name)

'those who LOVE (aheb) his name shall dwell in it' — the psalm's closing note: love for God's name marking those who inherit the saved Zion; aheb here the love of God's name that characterizes his true people - the lament of the drowning man ending in the settled love of the redeemed community

good (tob - your steadfast love is good)
v16: 'your steadfast love is GOOD (tob)' - the goodness of God's chesed (the qualifier, 281737); the quality on which the psalmist rests. Standalone (the quality).
v16: 'according to your ABUNDANT (rob) mercy' - the greatness of God's mercy (the qualifier, 281741). Standalone (the measure).
distress / trouble (tsar - for I am in distress)
v17: 'for I am in DISTRESS (tsar)' - the trouble that makes the psalmist beg God not to hide his face; his straits. Standalone (the distress).
soul (nefesh - draw near to my soul)
v18: 'Draw near to my SOUL (nefesh)' - the self God is asked to approach and redeem; the soul that pleads redemption. Standalone (the soul, object of God's drawing-near).
v19: 'You know my REPROACH (cherpah)' - the shame God fully knows; the psalmist's reproach laid bare before him (couple to the reproach-theme). Standalone (the reproach known to God).
v19: 'my SHAME (bosheth)' - the disgrace God knows; the psalmist's shame before his foes, all known to God. Standalone (the shame known to God).
v19: 'and my DISHONOR (kelimmah)' - the humiliation God knows; part of the reproach fully seen by him. Standalone (the dishonor known to God).
foes / adversaries (tsar - my foes are all known to you)
v19: 'my FOES (tsar) are all known to you' - the adversaries God fully knows; the enemies laid open before him. Standalone (the foes).
reproach (cherpah - reproaches have broken my heart)
v20: 'REPROACHES (cherpah) have broken my heart' - the scorn that shattered the psalmist's heart (the char, 281771); the wounding insults. Standalone (the reproaches that broke him).
v20: 'reproaches have BROKEN (shabar) my heart' - the breaking of the heart by scorn; the shattering carried in the broken-heart char (281771). Standalone (the breaking).
pity / sympathy (nud - I looked for pity, but there was none)
v20: 'I looked for PITY (nud), but there was none' - the sympathy the psalmist sought in vain; its absence deepening his despair (the char looked, 281773). Standalone (the absent pity).
comforters (nacham - for comforters, but I found none)
v20: 'and for COMFORTERS (nacham), but I found none' - the consolers who never came; the utter isolation of the sufferer. Standalone (the absent comforters).
v20: 'but I FOUND (matsa) none' - the vain search for comfort; no comforter to be found. Standalone (the not-finding).
poison / gall (rosh - they gave me poison for food)
v21: 'They gave me POISON (rosh) for food' - the gall the enemies gave instead of nourishment; the cruel mockery of his need (fulfilled at the cross, Matt 27:34). Standalone (the cruelty).
v21: 'poison for FOOD (barut)' - the nourishment the psalmist needed, given as gall; the mockery of his hunger. Standalone (the need mocked).
thirst (tsama - for my thirst they gave sour wine)

v21: 'for my THIRST (tsama) they gave me sour wine to drink' - the psalmist's thirst cruelly answered with vinegar; the need mocked (fulfilled at the cross, John 19:28-29). Standalone (the need mocked).
sour wine / vinegar (chomets - they gave me sour wine)
v21: 'they gave me SOUR WINE (chomets) to drink' - the vinegar given for thirst; the enemies' cruelty. Standalone (the cruelty).
give to drink (shaqah - sour wine to drink)
v21: 'sour wine to DRINK (shaqah)' - the giving of vinegar; the mocking of the psalmist's thirst. Standalone (the cruelty).
snare (pach - let their table become a snare)
v22: 'Let their own table before them become a SNARE (pach)' - the imprecation that the enemies' security turn to a trap; the fate invoked. Standalone (imprecation-fate, cited Rom 11:9).
peace / security (shalom - when they are at peace)
v22: 'when they are at PEACE (shalom), let it become a trap' - the enemies' false security, imprecated to become their snare; their complacency turned to ruin. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
trap / recompense (moqesh - let it become a trap)
v22: 'let it become a TRAP (moqesh)' - the snare invoked on the enemies; the imprecated recompense. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
be darkened (chashak - let their eyes be darkened)
v23: 'Let their eyes be DARKENED (chashak), so that they cannot see' - the imprecation of blindness on the enemies; the fate invoked (cited Rom 11:10). Standalone (imprecation-fate).
see (raah - so that they cannot see)
v23: 'so that they cannot SEE (raah)' - the blindness invoked on the enemies; the darkening of their eyes. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
tremble / shake (maad - make their loins tremble continually)
v23: 'make their loins TREMBLE (maad) continually' - the imprecation of unending weakness on the enemies; the fate invoked. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
camp / encampment (tirah - may their camp be a desolation)
v25: 'May their CAMP (tirah) be a desolation' - the imprecation that the enemies' dwelling be laid waste; the fate invoked (cited Acts 1:20). Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v25: 'may their camp be a DESOLATION (shamem); let no one dwell in their tents' - the imprecated ruin of the enemies' homes. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
persecute / pursue (radaph - they persecute him whom you have struck down)
v26: 'For they PERSECUTE (radaph) him whom you have struck down' - the enemies' cruelty in hounding the already-afflicted; the reason for the imprecation. Standalone (the enemies' cruelty).
strike (nakah - him whom you have struck down)
v26: 'him whom you have STRUCK DOWN (nakah)' - the afflicted one God has smitten, whom the enemies persecute the more; the sufferer's wounded state. Standalone (the afflicted state).
recount / tell (saphar - they recount the pain of those you wounded)
v26: 'they RECOUNT (saphar) the pain of those you have wounded' - the enemies gloating over the sufferings of the afflicted; their heartless mockery. Standalone (the enemies' cruelty).
pain / wound (makob - the pain of those you have wounded)
v26: 'the PAIN (makob) of those you have wounded' - the suffering of the afflicted, over which the enemies gloat; the wound the psalmist bears. Standalone (the suffering).
wound / pierce (chalal - those you have wounded)
v26: 'those you have WOUNDED (chalal)' - the afflicted whom God has pierced; the sufferers the enemies torment further. Standalone (the wounded).
iniquity / punishment (avon - add to them punishment)
v27: 'Add to them PUNISHMENT (avon) upon punishment' - the imprecation that guilt be heaped on the enemies; the fate invoked. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v27: 'punishment upon PUNISHMENT (avon)' - the doubled guilt/penalty imprecated on the enemies. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
righteousness / acquittal (tsedaqah - may they have no acquittal)
v27: 'may they have no ACQUITTAL (tsedaqah) from you' - the imprecation that the enemies find no vindication; denied righteousness before God. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
blot out (machah - let them be blotted out)
v28: 'Let them be BLOTTED OUT (machah) of the book of the living' - the imprecation that the enemies be erased from life; the fate invoked. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
book / register (sepher - the book of the living)
v28: 'the BOOK (sepher) of the living' - the register of life from which the enemies are imprecated to be blotted; the roll of the living. Standalone (image).
write / enroll (kathab - let them not be enrolled)

v28: 'let them not be ENROLLED (kathab) among the righteous' - the imprecation that the enemies not be numbered with the righteous; exclusion from the register of the just. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v28: 'let them not be enrolled among the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq)' - the company of the just from which the enemies are excluded; the register of the righteous. Standalone (the register of the righteous).
set on high (sagab - set me on high)
v29: 'let your salvation set me ON HIGH (sagab)' - the lifting-up the psalmist prays for; the security God's salvation (the qualifier) gives the afflicted (281812). Standalone (the outcome sought).
please / be good (yatab - this will please the LORD)

v31: 'This will PLEASE (yatab) the LORD more than an ox or a bull' - the praise pleasing God above sacrifice; the acceptableness of the psalmist's thanks (the char praise, 281826). Standalone (the pleasing of God).
ox / bull (shor - more than an ox)
v31: 'more than an OX (shor)' - the sacrificial animal the praise exceeds in pleasing God; the cultic offering surpassed by thanks. Standalone (cultic image).
bull / young ox (par - a bull with horns and hoofs)
v31: 'a BULL (par) with horns and hoofs' - the full-grown sacrifice the praise surpasses; the cultic offering exceeded by thanksgiving. Standalone (cultic image).
v31: 'a bull with HORNS (qaran)' - the mature bull's horns; part of the sacrificial image surpassed by praise. Standalone (image).
v31: 'a bull with horns and HOOFS (paras)' - the clean animal's cloven hoofs; part of the cultic image the praise exceeds. Standalone (image).
see (raah - when the humble see it)
v32: 'when the humble SEE (raah) it they will be glad' - the beholding of God's deliverance by the humble; the seeing that occasions their gladness (the char, 281838). Standalone (the beholding).
v32: 'let your HEARTS (lebab) revive' - the seat of the seekers' reviving life; the reviving is the char (281845, seat=heart). Standalone (the seat of the reviving).
praise (halal - let heaven and earth praise him)

v34: 'Let HEAVEN and earth PRAISE (halal) him, the seas and everything that moves in them' - the personified praise of all creation; the cosmos summoned to worship, not a human inner operation. Standalone (personification).
move / creep (ramas - everything that moves in the seas)
v34: 'and everything that MOVES (ramas) in them' - the sea-creatures summoned to praise; part of the cosmic call to worship. Standalone (personification).
build (banah - build up the cities of Judah)
v35: 'and BUILD UP (banah) the cities of Judah' - God's restoration of Judah's cities; the rebuilding that follows his saving of Zion (the qualifier save, 306609). Standalone (restoration outcome).
possess / inherit (yarash - people shall dwell there and possess it)
v35: 'and people shall dwell there and POSSESS (yarash) it' - the settling of the restored land; the outcome of God's salvation of Zion. Standalone (restoration outcome).
inherit (nachal - the offspring of his servants shall inherit it)

v36: 'The offspring of his servants shall INHERIT (nachal) it' - the servants' descendants receiving the restored Zion; the inheritance of the redeemed community, in which those who love God's name (281856) dwell. Standalone (the inheritance).
